title: Directives: v-if, v-for, v-model, and the key that matters

videos.script:
A directive is an attribute that starts with v dash. It tells the compiler to do something with the element it sits on. {{list}} This lesson is the ones you will type every day, and the one mistake each of them invites.

{{if}} v-if and v-show both hide things. One removes the element. The other only stops it being displayed. You will watch a component be built twice under one of them, and once under the other.

{{for}} v-for repeats an element. You will put a v-if beside it, the way old answers on the web suggest, and get an empty page.

{{key}} Then the key. Two lists, one star, and a removal. In one list the star moves to a course nobody starred.

{{model}} Then v-model, which joins a field to a ref in both directions. {{bind}} Then v-bind and v-on, with their shorthands and the modifiers that save you from the browser's defaults. {{own}} And a directive of your own, which focuses a field.

{{planner}} Last, the planner lists the week's sessions, and you tick one off.
